_comment: Gynaecology disease: pelvic organ prolapse. Same architecture as pneumonia and fibroid: almost every finding is an emphasis overlay on a shared core/obgyn skill. Prolapse's own contribution is supports and compartments, POP-Q staging against the hymen, bladder testing with the prolapse reduced, and pessary against uterus sparing or removing surgery as the management decision.

skill.particulars.demographics.expect: In suspected prolapse, age, parity and menopausal status carry real weight: an older multiparous postmenopausal woman starts with a high prior, while occupation with heavy lifting and residence far from theatre decide follow up and referral. Record fertility wishes with the particulars, since they frame every option later.

chapters.title: Patient particulars

chapters.blurb: A bulge that grows through the day, with bladder, bowel and conjugal symptoms

skill.hx.chief_complaints.expect: A typical presentation reads in years with a diurnal pattern: a bulge for years, worse through the day and on standing or straining, easing on lying down. That pattern alone should move you toward mechanical descent before anything else is known.

skill.hx.obg.gynae_symptoms.expect: Ask bladder, bowel and conjugal symptoms directly, since women often do not volunteer them: leaking on cough, incomplete emptying or the need to reduce the bulge to pass urine or stool, and discomfort during intercourse. Each maps to a compartment and to an operation.

chapters.title: History of presenting illness

chapters.blurb: Parity, pressure factors, fertility wishes and fitness

skill.hx.genital.risk.expect: Vaginal births, especially home deliveries and prolonged labour, plus chronic cough, constipation with straining, heavy lifting and obesity build the prior together. Fertility wishes and medical fitness then split the plan: preservation for the young, pessary for the unfit, definitive repair for the fit with completed family.

chapters.title: Past, personal, drug and family history

chapters.blurb: An elderly woman, often anaemic, with mobility that decides options

skill.gen.appearance.expect: Look for an elderly woman who walks slowly and may need help onto the couch: mobility and frailty decide pessary against surgery as much as the stage does. Pallor from chronic ulcer oozing and poor nutrition are common and must be corrected before any operation is dated.

skill.gen.vitals.expect: Expect normal vitals in uncomplicated prolapse: this is a chronic quality of life condition, not an acute illness. Hypertension, cardiac signs or poor effort tolerance matter because they raise anaesthetic risk and push the balance toward conservative care.

chapters.title: General examination

chapters.blurb: Which walls descend, how far past the hymen, and what the bladder does

skill.exam.obg.bimanual.expect: Expect a normal sized mobile uterus that moves with the cervix, with free fornices and no adnexal mass: descent with a normal uterus confirms prolapse rather than a pelvic tumour. A fixed mass, an enlarged uterus or a groove between mass and cervix points away from simple prolapse.

skill.exam.obg.gynae_abdominal.expect: The abdomen is usually normal in prolapse, and that negative is doing real work: it excludes a large pelvic mass pushing from above. Always examine with an empty bladder, since a full bladder mimics an anterior mass and confuses the pelvic findings.

skill.exam.obg.prolapse_popq.expect: Stage under maximal Valsalva in dorsal lithotomy with the bladder empty: record the six points against the hymen with total vaginal length, and repeat standing when the history is strong and lying shows little. Repeat the cough stress test with the prolapse reduced, since advanced descent can kink the urethra and hide stress leakage.

skill.exam.obg.speculum_inspect.expect: Note which walls descend and how far, the state of the cervix and vault, and any decubitus ulcer, discharge or bleeding on the exposed part. An ulcer or new bleeding needs care and exclusion of malignancy before staging is final and before any pessary goes in.

skill.exam.obg.vulval_inspect.expect: Expect a lax gaping introitus with a deficient perineum and the bulge appearing on bearing down. Perineal deficiency and levator laxity seen here explain recurrence risk and the need for perineal repair with any posterior wall surgery.

She asks to keep her uterus. Which operation preserves it, and what must you tell her about future pregnancy?

stations.title: Take a prolapse history and counsel on options

subtitle: POP-Q, conservative and surgical options

skill.prolapse.basics.oneLine: Descent of pelvic organs through weakened supports, staged by POP-Q

probes.a: Descent of the uterus, bladder, rectum or vault into or beyond the vagina from failure of pelvic supports.
probes.q: What is genital prolapse, in one sentence?

probes.a: Because symptoms follow the compartment: anterior descent disturbs the bladder while posterior descent obstructs the bowel.
probes.q: Why does the same disease give one woman leaking and another difficult emptying?

probes.a: A mechanical descent that gravity worsens through the day, typical of prolapse rather than a fixed mass.
probes.q: Her bulge is worst in the evening and gone each morning. What does that pattern tell you?

teach.body:
Level one suspends the apex: the cardinal and uterosacral ligaments hold the cervix and upper vagina. Level two attaches the mid vagina sideways to the pelvic wall through the pelvic fascia. Level three anchors the lower vagina in the perineum.

Vaginal birth stretches and denervates the levator muscles and these ligaments, and ageing, oestrogen loss and chronic pressure finish the job. Descent follows the weakest level, which is why one woman loses the front wall and another the apex.
teach.heading: Three levels hold everything up
Name it by compartment
points: Anterior: the bladder bulges into the front wall, called cystocele, with stress leakage and incomplete emptying.
Apical: the uterus descends, or the vault descends after hysterectomy; complete descent outside the introitus is called procidentia.
Posterior: the rectum bulges into the back wall, called rectocele, with difficult emptying and the need to press back.
Upper posterior: small bowel slides into the pouch between vagina and rectum, called enterocele, often with vault descent.

teach.body:
The constant thread is a bulge or dragging that grows through the day and with standing or straining, and eases on lying down.

Bladder, bowel and conjugal symptoms map to the compartment, and women often do not volunteer them: leaking on cough, needing to reduce the bulge to pass urine or stool, and discomfort during intercourse must each be asked directly.
teach.heading: Symptoms follow the compartment
What decides the course
points: Parity and menopause set the background: repeated vaginal birth injures supports, and oestrogen loss after the menopause thins them further.
Pressure decides the pace: cough, constipation, heavy lifting and obesity load weak supports every day.
Prior hysterectomy moves the risk to the vault, so a bulge after hysterectomy is staged for vault prolapse, not uterine descent.

skill.prolapse.basics.title: What genital prolapse is
skill.prolapse.basics.why: Prolapse is one of the commonest reasons an older parous woman meets a gynaecologist, and it ruins daily life long before it threatens it. The student who understands supports, compartments and staging can examine once and know the operation; the one who does not keeps describing a bulge.

skill.prolapse.signs.oneLine: What each compartment shows on examination and bedside testing

probes.a: A bulge that descends on bearing down and reduces on lying down, staged against the hymen.
probes.q: Which single finding separates prolapse from other vaginal lumps?

probes.a: Advanced prolapse can kink the urethra and hide stress leakage, which appears once the descent is reduced.
probes.q: Why repeat the cough test with the bulge pushed back?

probes.a: Acute retention with an irreducible mass needs urgent reduction and bladder drainage with prompt specialist review.
probes.q: She cannot pass urine and the prolapse is irreducible. What now?

teach.body:
Inspect the vulva and perineum with her bearing down: a lax introitus with a wall or the cervix appearing on strain is prolapse until proven otherwise.

Measure descent against the hymen under maximal strain in dorsal lithotomy. The hymen is the zero line of the POP-Q system, and every point is recorded as centimetres above or below it.
teach.heading: Look first, then measure
What each compartment shows
points: Cystocele: soft fullness of the front wall that descends on strain; ask about leak on cough and incomplete emptying alongside.
Uterine descent: the cervix presents at or beyond the introitus and moves with the uterus on bimanual examination; the exposed part may carry a decubitus ulcer or discharge.
Rectocele: bulging of the back wall with stool trapping; she may press the posterior wall or the perineum to finish passing stool.
Enterocele and vault prolapse: upper posterior fullness or a shortened vault after hysterectomy; examine standing as well as lying when the history is strong and lying shows little.

teach.heading: Three bedside tests that change the plan
points: Cough stress test with a comfortably full bladder: leakage synchronous with cough confirms stress incontinence, and repeat it with the prolapse reduced to unmask hidden leakage.
Post-void residual by catheter or ultrasound: raised residual means obstruction from the descent and must be known before bladder drugs or surgery.
Reducibility and ulcer check: note whether the mass reduces gently, and inspect the exposed tissue for ulcer, bleeding or infection that needs care before any pessary or operation.

skill.prolapse.signs.title: Putting the prolapse picture together
skill.prolapse.signs.why: The diagnosis is made with the eyes and a cough, not a scan: which wall descends, how far past the hymen, and what the bladder does when you reduce it. Miss the ulcer, the retention or the hidden leak, and the operation chosen is the wrong one.

skill.prolapse.summary.oneLine: One paragraph that carries compartment, stage and fitness

probes.a: Age, parity, menopausal state and fertility wishes, the bulge with duration and diurnal pattern, the compartment with the POP-Q stage, and bladder, bowel and ulcer status with fitness.
probes.q: What must a prolapse summary contain?

probes.a: Because fertility wishes choose preservation or removal, fitness chooses pessary or surgery, and incontinence testing decides whether a continence procedure joins the repair.
probes.q: Why do fertility wishes and fitness belong in the summary, not just the stage?

teach.body:
Open with age, parity, menopausal state and fertility wishes: a 58 year old postmenopausal para four with completed family. Then the bulge with duration and diurnal pattern.

Then the findings in one line: compartment, POP-Q points and stage, with bladder, bowel and ulcer status. Close with fitness for surgery and the provisional plan.
teach.heading: The shape of the summary

teach.body:
A 58 year old postmenopausal para four with a three year bulge worse through the day. Examination shows uterine descent with cystocele and rectocele, POP-Q stage three, with stress leakage and a small decubitus ulcer, fit for surgery.

The plan is vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair and continence assessment, after ulcer healing and iron correction.
teach.heading: A worked example
What students leave out
points: Incontinence type: stress, urgency or hidden leakage decides whether a continence procedure joins the repair.
Ulcer, bleeding or irreducibility: each changes timing and needs care before staging is final.
Fertility wishes and fitness: preservation against removal, and pessary against surgery, hang on these two facts.

skill.prolapse.summary.title: Summarising the prolapse case
skill.prolapse.summary.why: A summary that carries compartment, stage, incontinence and fitness hands the consultant the whole decision in one paragraph. One that only describes a bulge sends her back for the examination you should already have done.

skill.prolapse.differential.oneLine: Fibroid polyp, inversion, vault descent and the three incontinences

probes.a: A fibroid polyp comes through the cervical os with a normal sized uterus above, while prolapse descends with the uterus; the sound passes beside a polyp.
probes.q: How do you separate a fibroid polyp from prolapse at the bedside?

probes.a: Stress leakage is synchronous with cough and effort, urgency leakage follows a sudden compelling desire to void, and overflow is continuous dribbling from a full bladder.
probes.q: A woman leaks urine. How do you sort stress from urgency from overflow?

probes.a: A dimpled fundus felt abdominally with no uterus above the mass means chronic inversion, which is replaced rather than excised or suspended.
probes.q: The mass looks like procidentia but no uterus is felt above it. What have you missed?

sources.locator: Differential diagnosis of pelvic organ prolapse

rows: Firm mass through the cervical os with a normal sized uterus above; the sound passes beside it
Cup shaped dimple of the fundus felt abdominally with no uterus above the mass
Small tense vaginal wall cyst that does not descend further on straining
Tender anterior swelling with dribbling and past infections, unlike soft cystocele

teach.heading: Incontinence has three faces
points: Stress: leakage synchronous with cough, laugh or effort from weak support or sphincter; confirmed by cough stress test.
Urgency: leakage preceded by a sudden compelling desire to void from an overactive detrusor; treated first with bladder training and bladder relaxants.
Overflow: continuous dribbling from a full poorly emptying bladder; check residual before calling it stress, since bladder relaxants worsen retention.

teach.body:
After hysterectomy the same bulge is vault prolapse or enterocele, not uterine descent, and the repair is vault suspension rather than hysterectomy.

High rectocele and enterocele overlap on examination; the enterocele sits higher in the posterior wall and often accompanies vault descent.
teach.heading: Post-hysterectomy and high mimics

skill.prolapse.differential.title: What else a vaginal bulge can be
skill.prolapse.differential.why: Most bulges are prolapse, but the exceptions operate completely differently: a fibroid polyp needs excision, an inversion needs replacement, a diverticulum needs urology. The bedside tests that separate them take a minute and save a wrong operation.

skill.ix.prolapse.workup.oneLine: Stage it on examination, test the bladder, image only what changes care

probes.a: POP-Q examination in dorsal lithotomy under maximal Valsalva, recording six points against the hymen with total vaginal length.
probes.q: How is prolapse staged?

probes.a: Urine test, bladder diary, cough stress test with the prolapse reduced, post-void residual, and pad testing to quantify leakage.
probes.q: What bladder assessment does every prolapse need?

probes.a: Urodynamics for mixed, recurrent or post-repair leakage and pre-surgical doubt; renal tract views in procidentia for hydronephrosis.
probes.q: When do you order urodynamics, and when renal imaging?

sources.locator: Pelvic organ prolapse: assessment and management
sources.source: NICE guideline: Urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse in women

teach.body:
POP-Q examination in dorsal lithotomy under maximal Valsalva records six points against the hymen and assigns the stage; it is repeated standing when the history is strong and lying shows little.

Record total vaginal length and genital hiatus with the points, since the repair is planned from these numbers and they are the baseline if prolapse recurs in another compartment.
teach.heading: Examination is the investigation
Test the bladder in every case
points: Urine test and culture to exclude infection before any bladder interpretation or operation.
Frequency volume diary kept over days to separate stress from urgency and mixed patterns.
Cough stress test with a comfortably full bladder, repeated with the prolapse reduced to unmask hidden leakage.
Post-void residual by catheter or ultrasound: raised residual signals obstruction and must precede bladder drugs.
Pad test to quantify leakage where severity decides between conservative and surgical care.

teach.body:
Multichannel urodynamics with cystometry and leak point pressure is reserved for mixed or recurrent leakage, failed prior repair, or pre-surgical doubt about the incontinence type.

Pelvic ultrasound characterises an atypical mass, and renal tract views are added in procidentia to exclude hydronephrosis from ureteric kinking; cervical screening and basic fitness tests complete the pre-operative set.
teach.heading: When to go further

skill.ix.prolapse.workup.title: Investigating prolapse and incontinence
skill.ix.prolapse.workup.why: Prolapse is staged by examination, not by scan, and the investigations that matter are the ones that change the operation: bladder function, residual urine, the upper tract in advanced disease, and fitness for theatre. Ordering a scan first and examining second is the expensive way round.

skill.prolapse.diagnosis.oneLine: Compartment plus POP-Q stage plus incontinence type

probes.a: The compartment with the structure behind it, the POP-Q stage from the leading edge, and the bladder state: continent, stress, urgency, mixed or hidden leakage.
probes.q: What are the three parts of a complete prolapse diagnosis?

probes.a: Stage three: the leading edge lies more than 1 cm beyond the hymen but short of complete eversion.
probes.q: The leading edge is 4 cm beyond the hymen with a vaginal length of 8 cm. What stage is this?

probes.a: New bleeding needs malignancy excluded, retention needs drainage, and loin pain with procidentia needs renal tract views for hydronephrosis.
probes.q: Which findings block routine staging and force urgent review?

teach.body:
First the compartment: anterior, apical or posterior, with the structure behind it. Second the POP-Q stage from the leading edge. Third the bladder: continent, stress, urgency, mixed or hidden leakage.

A complete diagnosis reads as one line: uterine descent with cystocele and rectocele, POP-Q stage three, with stress urinary incontinence.
teach.heading: The diagnosis has three parts
Stages in plain words
points: Stage zero: no descent beyond the normal position.
Stage one: the leading edge is still well inside, more than 1 cm above the hymen.
Stage two: the leading edge sits around the hymen, within 1 cm on either side.
Stage three: the leading edge is more than 1 cm beyond the hymen but short of complete eversion.
Stage four: complete eversion or procidentia of the lower tract.

teach.body:
Atrophy, ulcer and residual urine are recorded with the stage since each changes timing: ulcer and infection need healing first, and raised residual needs drainage before drugs.

New bleeding, an irreducible mass, retention or loin pain block routine staging and need urgent review for malignancy, obstruction or renal involvement.
teach.heading: What completes and what blocks the diagnosis

skill.prolapse.diagnosis.title: Diagnosing and staging prolapse
skill.prolapse.diagnosis.why: Compartment plus stage plus bladder state is the whole diagnosis, and it is also the whole operative plan: the compartment chooses the repair, the stage chooses pessary against surgery, and the bladder decides whether a continence procedure joins it.

skill.tx.prolapse.dosingNote: This module teaches management at the level of method and principle, with drug classes named without doses. Specific agents, regimens and doses must be taken from your current national or institutional guideline at the time of prescribing. CliniX does not prescribe.
skill.tx.prolapse.oneLine: Physiotherapy and pessary first, uterus sparing or removing surgery matched to wishes

probes.a: Supervised pelvic floor muscle training with weight, cough and constipation addressed.
probes.q: What is first line for mild prolapse?

probes.a: When she declines surgery, is unfit, awaits surgery, is pregnant, or wishes to preserve fertility, with regular review.
probes.q: When is a pessary the right answer?

probes.a: Vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair, adding a midurethral sling once testing confirms stress incontinence.
probes.q: Completed family, stage three prolapse with a proven stress leak. What operation?

sources.locator: Pelvic organ prolapse: assessment and management
sources.source: NICE guideline: Urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse in women

teach.body:
Supervised pelvic floor muscle training suits mild to moderate prolapse and is first line alongside lifestyle change: weight reduction, treatment of cough and constipation, and lighter lifting.

Review symptoms and stage at follow up; training that fails over months, or prolapse that advances despite it, moves the discussion to mechanical support or surgery.
teach.heading: Start without surgery

teach.body:
Offer a pessary to women who decline surgery, are unfit for it, await it, or need support in pregnancy or while fertility is preserved. Ring devices suit most vault and wall descent; shelf, Gellhorn, cube and donut types hold where tone is poor.

Teach insertion, removal and cleaning with review once in three months. Watch for discharge, erosion, ulcer, bleeding and impaction, and avoid pessaries with undiagnosed bleeding, vaginal cancer or active infection.
teach.heading: The pessary: who, which and how

teach.body:
Vaginal oestrogen improves atrophic tissue and protects the mucosa in postmenopausal pessary users.

Urgency with detrusor overactivity is treated first with bladder training, then bladder relaxant drugs of the antimuscarinic or beta-3 agonist classes; stress leakage failing training may be offered duloxetine where surgery is not chosen. No doses are quoted here: take every regimen from the current guideline at prescribing.
teach.heading: Oestrogen and bladder medicines

teach.body:
Uterus sparing repair suits younger women: the Manchester operation corrects descent with cervical amputation and ligament fixation, with anterior and posterior repair added as needed.

With completed family, vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair removes the uterus and suspends the vault; wall defects are repaired by plicating the pubocervical fascia in front and the rectovaginal fascia with perineal repair behind, with cul-de-sac obliteration for enterocele.
teach.heading: Operations: preserve or remove

teach.body:
Stress incontinence with prolapse is treated by midurethral sling placed retropubically or through the obturator route, with bladder injury excluded by cystoscopy; confirm the leak type with testing before adding a sling to any repair.

Frail women who no longer desire intercourse may be offered colpocleisis, and sacrospinous fixation or abdominal sacrocolpopexy suspend the vault where vaginal repair cannot hold.
teach.heading: Continence surgery and the frail woman

teach.body:
Pessary care, physiotherapy and ulcer healing belong at every hospital; vaginal hysterectomy with floor repair and Manchester surgery at centres with a gynaecology theatre.

Refer promptly for irreducible procidentia, retention, hydronephrosis, recurrent vault prolapse, suspected mesh complication, or incontinence that urodynamics must sort before surgery.
teach.heading: Indian context and referral thresholds

skill.tx.prolapse.title: Managing genital prolapse
skill.tx.prolapse.why: Most prolapse can be managed without an operation, and the operation when needed is chosen by fertility wishes and fitness, not by stage alone. A young woman sterilised by an unnecessary hysterectomy and an unfit woman harmed by one are the two errors this chapter exists to prevent.

diagnosis.answer: Pelvic organ prolapse: uterine descent with cystocele and rectocele, POP-Q stage III, with stress urinary incontinence and a decubitus ulcer.

differentialModel.answer: Uterine descent with cystocele and rectocele (POP-Q stage III) with stress urinary incontinence. Consider enterocele, fibroid polyp, chronic uterine inversion, and urgency incontinence as a mixed component.

skill.exam.obg.bimanual.finding: Uterus normal sized, mobile, moving with the cervix. Both fornices free, no adnexal mass, no cervical motion tenderness.

skill.exam.obg.gynae_abdominal.finding: No palpable mass and the uterus is not felt abdominally. No organomegaly and the hernial orifices are free.

skill.exam.obg.prolapse_popq.finding: POP-Q with maximal strain: Aa +2, Ba +3, C +4, D +2, Ap +1, Bp +2, vaginal length 8 cm. Leading edge C at +4: stage III. Cough stress test leaks with the prolapse reduced.

skill.exam.obg.speculum_insert.finding: Speculum passed without difficulty and the blades opened to reveal the descent.

skill.exam.obg.speculum_inspect.finding: Uterine descent with cystocele and rectocele. The cervix lies at the introitus with a 2 cm decubitus ulcer and mucoid discharge on the exposed lip.

skill.exam.obg.vulval_inspect.finding: Lax gaping introitus with a deficient perineum. A moist mass presents on bearing down and reduces on lying down.

skill.gen.appearance.finding: Alert 58 year old, moderately built, no pallor and no distress at rest. She walks slowly but without support.

skill.gen.vitals.finding: Pulse 84, blood pressure 130/80, afebrile. No postural symptoms on standing.

cases.fallback: I am not sure what you mean, doctor. Can you ask that a different way?

cues: do you leak urine on coughing
urine escapes when you laugh or lift
how often do you change cloth for leaking
bladder_leak.reply: When I cough or lift a water pot, a little urine escapes. I wear an extra cloth on work days.

cues: need to press near the back passage to empty
how often do you strain for stool
bowel_emptying.reply: I strain for stool and sometimes press near the back passage to finish. Motions come every two to three days and are hard.

cues: when did the bulge first appear
does the mass come out on standing
does lying down reduce the swelling
how has the descent progressed over time
bulge_course.reply: It started as a small heaviness after my last delivery, twenty years ago. Now it comes out every day on standing and goes back when I lie down at night.

conjugal_life.reply: Intercourse has been painful and difficult for years because of the bulge, so we have stopped. Sometimes urine escapes then.

cues: long standing cough in your history
cough_constipation_load.reply: I have had a morning cough for years from cooking smoke. I strain daily for stool. I carry headloads of fodder, and my weight has risen.

discharge_bleed.reply: There is a white discharge that stains my clothes, and last month the outer part bled a little when I scratched it. No heavy bleeding.

cues: tablets for urine or bowel complaints
drug_allergy.reply: I take no regular tablets and have used no hormones. No allergy that I know.

cues: similar complaint in mother or sisters
who cooks with wood smoke at home
family_home.reply: My mother had the same trouble in old age. We cook on wood. My son and his wife live with us, and there is a latrine at home now.

medical_past.reply: No sugar or pressure that I know. No operation. I take no regular tablets.

cues: at what age did periods stop
were your periods regular before stopping
menstrual_past.reply: Periods stopped ten years ago, at 48. They were regular before that.

cues: how many normal deliveries have you had
babies born heavy or with instruments
obstetric_past.reply: Four normal deliveries, all at home, the last two long labours. No operation, no abortion. The babies were healthy.

cues: dragging pain in the lower abdomen
backache that worsens through the day
heaviness that eases on lying down
pelvic_heaviness.reply: There is a dragging ache low in the stomach and in the back by evening. Lying down relieves it.

cues: how many meals do you eat
personal_habits.reply: I use mishri on the gums twice a day. Two meals, little water while working. Sleep breaks twice to pass urine.

cues: why have you come to hospital
tell me your trouble in your own words
presenting.reply: Doctor, for three years something comes down from below when I stand and work. By evening it hangs out, and in the morning it goes back inside.

cues: treatment taken for this bulge before
why did you come to hospital now
prior_care.reply: A local doctor gave ointment for the sore on the outer part. No ring or operation was advised. I came now because the sore bleeds and the bulge stays out longer.

cues: need to push the bulge back to urinate
going again soon after passing urine
voiding_strain.reply: The stream is slow, and on bad days I press the bulge back with my fingers to pass urine fully.

fbc.label: Full blood count
fbc.note: Mild iron deficiency from chronic ulcer oozing: correct with iron before any operation is dated.
fbc.result: Haemoglobin 10 g per dL with microcytic indices; white cells and platelets normal.

pap.label: Cervical screening
pap.note: Mandatory before uterus sparing or removing surgery to exclude cervical disease.

pvr.label: Post-void residual by ultrasound
pvr.note: Raised residual confirms obstruction from the descent; reassess after reduction and before bladder drugs.
pvr.result: Residual urine of 150 mL after voiding.

urine_routine.label: Urine routine and culture
urine_routine.note: Excludes infection before bladder testing and surgery.
urine_routine.result: Trace protein, no pus cells, culture sterile.

usg_pelvic.label: Pelvic and renal ultrasound
usg_pelvic.note: Excludes a pelvic mass that mimics descent and checks the upper tract in advanced prolapse.
usg_pelvic.result: Uterus normal sized with descent; ovaries atrophic; no mass or free fluid; mild fullness of both renal pelves without frank hydronephrosis.

managementModel.answer: Heal the ulcer first with reduction, hygiene and vaginal oestrogen, correct the iron deficiency, and test continence with the prolapse reduced. Family is complete and she is fit, so plan vaginal hysterectomy with pelvic floor repair with a sling if stress leakage is confirmed; counsel the pessary as the alternative.

cases.opening: Kamala Devi, 58, a farm labourer from a village near Kolhapur, walks in slowly with her daughter-in-law. She keeps her eyes down. Introduce yourself and take a history.

patient.name: Kamala Devi
patient.residence: Rural, lives with her husband, son and daughter-in-law

teachingPoints: The diurnal pattern is the diagnosis before you examine: a bulge that grows through the day and reduces on lying down is mechanical descent, not a fixed tumour.
